summary: New box Part. Pass.: example for sense 1 in Part. Pass. (PrS 71/37)

data.turoyo: Kit žənnəke bu bayto ʕayna kḥile, mamṭela u laḥmo šaḥino mu farmo.
data.translation: In dem Hause war eine Frau mit geschminkten Augen, eben hatte sie das Brot warm aus dem Ofen genommen.

rationale: New Detransitive Part. Pass. box; painted eyes as result-state modifier, one attestation.

data.turoyo: <...> Kətwo kəḥliwo ʕaynayye ste šafiro, buwwe.
data.translation: <...> There were people who also painted their eyes properly with it.

summary: New box Infectum-wa: example for sense 1 in Infectum-wa (Jan 2.5/1587)

data.turoyo: Xori Brahim: Meqəm kəḥliwo, yabo! I haymonuṯaṯṯe hawxa əmmowalle. Ham gədnayḥi mu kewo ste w ham bi haymonuṯaṯṯe, d kətyo kuḥlo d Mšiḥo, hawxa.
data.translation: Khori Brahim: Before, they used to paint their eyes, my dear! That is how they described their faith. Both that they would get relief from the pain, and in their faith too, that it is Christ's kohl, like that.

rationale: Second Infectum-wa example; reported medicinal and religious purposes remain contextual motivations, not new senses.

summary: New box Infectum-wa: example for sense 1 in Infectum-wa (Jan 3.45/1250)

data.turoyo: Ǧan: Abuna, koṯe l bolxo yawmo d Maʕəlṯo, maydituwo aš šamʕe w nəfqituwo l larwal? W kətwo ʕade kəḥliwo ʕaynoṯayye, qay kəḥliwo ʕaynoṯayye?
data.translation: Jan: Father, do you remember Candlemas day, when you used to take the candles and go outside? And there was a custom: they used to blacken their eyes. Why did they used to blacken their eyes?

rationale: Third Infectum-wa example; Candlemas question anchors the ritual context and preserves the plural ʕaynoṯayye.

summary: New box Infectum-wa: example for sense 1 in Infectum-wa (Jan 3.45/1251)

data.turoyo: Xori ʕAziz: E, kəḥlənwanne. ʕAde wa, kəḥlənwanne.
data.translation: Father Aziz: Yes, they used to blacken them. It was a custom; they used to blacken them.

rationale: Fourth Infectum-wa example; plural patient indexing in kəḥlənwanne contrasts with the free eye noun.

summary: New box Infectum-wa: example for sense 1 in Infectum-wa (Jan 3.45/1253)

data.turoyo: <...> Lo koḏaʕno, elo kəḥliwa ʕaynayye, əmmiwa, ʕal d howən ʕaynayye šafire. <...>
data.translation: <...> I do not know, but they would blacken their eyes; they used to say, so that their eyes would become beautiful. <...>

rationale: Fifth Infectum-wa example; purpose clause and -wa variant complement the religious account.

summary: example for sense 2 in Preterit (95/243)

data.turoyo: Məlle: “Rawixo, mə šəkəl yo?” Məlla: “Xort yarixo, rafiʕo, u səsyaḏe kab raš yo, henu mkaḥalle la šwarfayḏe, hawo, d moṭelux, azze menux.”
data.translation: Wie sieht denn der Reiter aus? Es ist ein Junger, langer, dünner Bursch; sein Pferd hat schwarze Flecken auf den knieen; sein schnurrhart ist eben erst gesproßt. Wenner dich erreicht, so ist es um dich geschehen. -

rationale: Thin existing II.2 Preterit cell; explicit incipient moustache growth with l-marked body-part NP.

summary: Active self-grooming takes the subject’s possessed eyes as patient, without ruḥo or Detransitive morphology. The k of kəḥli is a root consonant, not automatically an indicative prefix.

PrS 71/37 noun phrase ʕayna kḥile gives a plural painted-state modifier, whereas 29/55 has a finite active painting predicate followed by its eye object. One secure noun-phrase context supports the new box, pending morphological confirmation.

II.2 already lexicalizes moustache sprouting. Incipient henu/žhenu and variable l-marking do not create a new sense or establish the precise suffix segmentation. No new idiomatic phrase is established.

Round 2, Jan Beṯ-Şawoce. English quotations below reproduce the supplied project machine translation, not an edition translation. Analyses and sense distinctions rest on the Turoyo. Round-one proposals are retained as the comparison baseline and are not republished in this JSON.
Jan supplies the previously absent I Infectum-wa box, with -wo/-wa and -nne patient indexing. The first k belongs to the root; these are not automatically double-prefixed forms.
Possessed eyes or an object suffix code the patient. Coreference with the painter does not make these Detransitive, and the round-one Detransitive Part. Pass. proposal is not repeated.
The beauty and pain-relief explanations are speakers' reports; no efficacy claim or additional lexical meaning is inferred. No light-verb noun construction or fixed idiom is established.
Confirm the vowel length and plural Part. Pass. interpretation of kḥile at PrS 71/37.
Does kəḥli/kuḥli reflect phonetic or editorial variation?
How should mkaḥalle with a plural moustache NP and alternating l-marking be segmented? Keep inherited II Preterit filing pending confirmation.
Confirm person/suffix segmentation in kəḥlənwanne and whether -wo/-wa variation is dialectal or editorial.
Are the religious and cosmetic applications named differently by speakers? The evidence currently supports one verb sense only.
Adults, children, Candlemas participants and believers seeking pain relief all perform the same eye-painting action; no ritual or medical subsense is established.
